suites.name: two-worker-smoke
suites.intro: Run before a release (never on a schedule) from the ServerWorker worker with DesktopWorker online; swap roles for a second pass when both are available. Each check maps to a bug the owner previously found by hand (session titles in brackets).

rows.how: GET deploy-status
rows.pass_when: both workers listed by name (not a hex id), revisions shown
rows.past_bug: ServerWorker shows as a bunch of numbers

rows.how: start a session on the peer: "Live test {run}: reply with the single word OK and use no tools."
rows.pass_when: REST transcript contains a non-empty assistant reply after the prompt, the turn finishes and the session is owned by the peer (no wording requirement)
rows.past_bug: error when starting a session on another worker

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word OK and use no tools.

rows.how: browser: open a peer session while it runs `sleep 60`
rows.pass_when: Stop button visible and stops the turn
rows.past_bug: Stop button doesn't show on sessions created on another worker

rows.how: browser: start a peer session with a small image attached
rows.pass_when: model describes the image; no purge error
rows.past_bug: attach an image when starting a session from one worker to another

rows.how: ask a peer session to write `hello.txt` and link it
rows.pass_when: link downloads from this worker's UI
rows.past_bug: Chat downloads error from a remote worker

rows.how: ask a peer session to open example.com with the browser tools
rows.pass_when: this worker's browser panel shows the peer's page
rows.past_bug: browser panel does not show remote worker's browser

rows.how: owner powers the peer off, then settles its session from this worker
rows.pass_when: settle succeeds, syncs on reconnect
rows.past_bug: can't settle sessions for a worker that's offline

rows.how: (only when a throwaway PR exists) open the Git panel on the remote session
rows.pass_when: PR state correct, no "Git unavailable"
rows.past_bug: ship it shows git unavailable (x3)

rows.how: start two throwaway chats, then dispatch a peer message with owner authority on local ingress (require_admin), using a stable request id, and poll its durable receipt
rows.pass_when: MessageSession is in the available tool catalog; the same receiver turn id reaches consumed (queued, begun or stopped alone never pass); no model wording or tool-choice requirement
rows.past_bug: message only delivered after session fully completed

steps.prompt: Live test {run} A: reply briefly, no tools.
Live test {run} B: reply briefly, no tools.

steps.message: Live smoke {run}: delivery probe; no reply required.

rows.how: a local session starts a background subagent on the peer, messages it after it finishes (resume), then starts and stops a second one
rows.pass_when: Task, SendMessage and TaskStop all used; reply SUBAGENT-DONE
rows.past_bug: subagents on another worker could not be messaged, stopped or resumed

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: keep every subagent prompt tiny. 1) Use Task with worker "{peer}" and mode background to start any coding subagent from your roster with the prompt "reply with the single word SUB-OK, no tools". 2) When it reports, use SendMessage to that agent with "reply with the single word SUB-AGAIN, no tools" and wait for its report. 3) Use Task with worker "{peer}" and mode background again with the prompt "run sleep 300 in Bash", then stop it at once with TaskStop. Then reply with just: SUBAGENT-DONE

rows.how: send a second message the moment the first reply appears
rows.pass_when: two user bubbles, one ONE reply and one TWO reply (nothing lost, nothing doubled)
rows.past_bug: a message sent as a turn ended was lost or shown twice

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word ONE and use no tools.
Reply with the single word TWO and use no tools.

rows.check: Prompt card in an open chat
rows.how: open a chat through the preview port; ask it to use AskUserQuestion with two options
rows.pass_when: the card renders in the open chat, an answer reaches the turn
rows.past_bug: prompt cards did not appear in an already-open chat

rows.how: one reply, then /compact through the API, then one more reply
rows.pass_when: compact boundary recorded, the next message still answers
rows.past_bug: /compact failed or lost the session

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word OK and use no tools.
Reply with the single word AGAIN and use no tools.

rows.check: Image edit on the configured provider
rows.how: editImage on a 4x4 PNG the runner writes (one paid image call)
rows.pass_when: editImage used; reply EDITED
rows.past_bug: image edit failed on the configured provider

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: use the editImage tool once on the image at {image} with the prompt "make it red". Then reply with just: EDITED

rows.how: owner quits the desktop app on the peer and starts it again
rows.pass_when: the peer comes back online and its sessions open from this worker
rows.past_bug: desktop app did not come back cleanly after quit

rows.check: Android voice call lock and unlock
rows.how: On a physical phone running the branch APK and a worker serving the branch UI, start a GPT Live call in a throwaway chat. Lock for 10 seconds, unlock, and speak again. Repeat after rotating the phone while locked and after changing system light/dark mode. Archive the throwaway chat after ending the call. Capture adb logcat for activity recreation or renderer loss and the worker voice/SSE logs.
rows.pass_when: The same call hears and replies after each unlock; no audio close with code 1006, cold from_seq=0 feed connection, activity recreation or WebView renderer loss during the cycle.
rows.past_bug: #1969: locking kept voice alive but unlocking destroyed the page and audio socket

rows.how: On disposable paired workers only, restore one worker's device keys into a fresh data directory with a new install id. Wait for its signed presence to reach the peer; pick it for a chat and read its Git state. Join a third disposable worker and confirm it waits for fresh signed presence before resolving the new id. Do not change live worker identities.
rows.pass_when: the peer resolves the new install id to the original device, names it correctly and routes chat/Git control there; the certificate's old id still works; a snapshot alone never authorizes the second alias
rows.past_bug: #1716: a stale membership install id made peer-side lookups miss an active worker

rows.how: start an owner Claude session on each worker; ask it to open the running UI using the preview link in its workspace facts, without reading key files; wait for the sidebar data to load
rows.pass_when: both sessions receive a working session-bound link; the desktop link uses loopback; the preview lists the same visible active chats and agents as the owner's UI (Active counts chats, not links or hidden workers)
rows.past_bug: #1789: delegated sessions received no preview link; desktop links named an unreachable LAN address; an initial Active 0 needed tracing

rows.how: On disposable workers only: sync a chat with 100 events, take its peer offline, restart the owner, append 400 events while its outbox is held, then bring the peer back. Repeat with reversed dial direction. Open Settings > Devices > This worker during catch-up. Also repeat from a backup whose stream head is behind the peer.
rows.pass_when: The 400-event delta arrives on first safe contact in seconds, with no historical republish, seven 64-or-fewer-event receiver batches and ordered seq 1..500. Devices shows Syncing during apply and Ready afterwards. A restored owner keeps the hold until signed rollback proof is checked and advances its incarnation before publishing.
rows.past_bug: A restarted owner held writes until reconnect, then catch-up left the open chat stale for minutes with no progress status.

rows.how: On an existing idle large chat, type a draft and press Send. Do not choose Send anyway or Compact first: leave the model idle. Check the warning at desktop and phone widths against GET /sessions/{id}/cache-state, then clear the draft.
rows.pass_when: Before any turn starts, both API-price totals appear, compact-and-continue equals compaction plus continuation, assumptions and the cheaper-option recommendation are shown; unpriced models say unavailable rather than free.
rows.past_bug: #1831: the cold-send warning did not include the cost of compaction in its comparison

rows.check: Indexed SessionSearch on real worker history
rows.how: After updating, check recall in the default legacy-index mode first. Only with separate owner approval, schedule offline maintenance on a worker and run python -m app.maintenance.session_recall_cache --apply (from the installed source, with the worker's interpreter); do not run it while workers serve traffic. Then create throwaway native and delegated chats locally and a chat on the peer, each containing the same unique three-word marker. From another throwaway chat use SessionSearch to recall the marker and view each hit. rows.check: Task bases respect hotfix callers and explicit pins
rows.how: On disposable paired candidate workers, register a temporary repository whose origin/main is ahead of a hotfix/1.2 branch with no unique commits and no default upstream. Dispatch coding Tasks locally and to the peer from a chat bound to hotfix/1.2; then repeat from main and from a branch tracking origin/main. Repeat with an explicit old base_commit and a deliberately slow origin (more than five but less than sixty seconds) for a new chat. Do not alter production repository refs.
rows.pass_when: Hotfix Tasks on both workers retain the caller SHA and cannot merge unreleased main commits into hotfix. Default/tracking callers use fresh origin/main only when it contains the caller. Explicit pins trigger no fetch. A new chat waits for the slow successful fetch and starts at the new origin tip; missing dispatch receipts leave remote branches untouched with an honest reason.
rows.past_bug: #407: ancestry alone refreshed non-default callers, chat fetches timed out after five seconds, explicit pins fetched unnecessarily, and missing receipts blamed branch movement.

rows.check: Peer terminal consent survives only retryable folder checks
rows.how: On disposable paired candidate workers, enable peer terminals in owner policy and approve one shell on the recipient using matching panel codes. Enter an invalid folder, correct it and open with the same approval. Repeat with a folder moved during spawn, and revoke the requester lease during a deliberately delayed recipient folder check. Finally open a shell and turn policy off on the source only without polling source authorization status. Inspect recipient PTY creation/closure and source leases; exercise input/output, resize, reload/reconnect and close through the panel.
rows.pass_when: Pre-spawn folder refusal retains approval and correction works. A spawn-time folder race forgets the source lease, drops recipient consent and asks for new approval instead of promising a folder retry. Revoke during folder validation creates no PTY. Source-only policy-off refuses the recipient callback and ends the live shell within its fifteen-second authorization recheck plus callback time, without waiting for a status GET or ten-minute expiry.
rows.past_bug: #378: a spawn-time folder race kept a dead lease, requester revoke during folder validation spawned a PTY, and source-only policy-off retained callback authority.

rows.check: Active-only worktree status and idle edits
rows.how: On a disposable candidate install, prepare a project with 100 non-retired historical worktrees (sessions inactive for over three hours) and three active worktrees: one focused, one recently used, and one streaming. Restart only the disposable install to clear its in-memory status cache. Refresh the worktree list repeatedly and record actual git status reader calls and status_checked_at fields. Focus a previously unchecked historical checkout once, then leave it inactive. In a recently active but idle checkout, edit a tracked file outside an agent turn, wait for the file-event debounce, and refresh the list. Repeat after adding a directory and editing a file inside it. Open the same project in two clients focused on different checkouts and alternate polls, including requests with no focus; edit files in both checkouts. Stop renewing only one focus and confirm only its watch expires after the lease; finally leave the project and confirm all watches expire. Do not use production data or restart installed workers.
rows.pass_when: Cold and repeated refreshes read only the three active checkouts, not the 100 historical ones. Unchecked rows retain null status and status_checked_at until focused; previously checked inactive rows retain their last status. Idle edits, including in new directories, appear with a newer status_checked_at after debounce without a turn-end hook. Native watches exclude nested worktrees and dependency trees. Concurrent clients retain independent per-path leases: another client's different or missing focus cannot cancel a live watch, and only unrenewed paths stop after expiry.
rows.past_bug: #436: every unseen historical worktree received a cold status scan, and idle file edits had no debounced status invalidation.

rows.check: Native wake provenance across context pruning and rewind/resume
rows.how: On a disposable candidate install, start a throwaway native-provider chat. Produce ordinary user turns, a background-task wake and a peer-delivered turn, including assistant tool calls/results. Record their first persisted TurnStarted sources and node IDs using a read-only diagnostic that emits only synthetic IDs, sources, replay cursors and decoded-row counts. Compact enough history to prune those nodes from the live context, then rewind to each recorded user/wake/peer node and resume it. Repeat an unchanged context scan and append a fresh user turn after an assistant/tool exchange. Archive only the throwaway chat and remove only diagnostics created for this check; never restart or mutate the installed worker or dump prompts, credentials or provider payloads.
rows.pass_when: Returning nodes retain their FIRST TurnStarted source despite later resume events: user turns stay user-authored and wake/peer turns keep their original exemptions and wake-aware counting. Only re-entering pruned context replays provenance from zero. Unchanged context and newly appended turns keep the saved cursor and decode only newer matching events, not the historical prefix or large tool results. Examined-node and provenance bookkeeping are pruned to the active context plus nodes appended since its last scan. Missing live evidence is recorded as not_run, not pass.
rows.past_bug: #354 / #264 / PR #504: unbounded wake bookkeeping required pruning, but comparing all active context nodes with only TurnStarted-named nodes restarted full provenance replay on ordinary mixed-role turns.

rows.check: Monitor viewer disconnect preserves its running shell
rows.how: On a real candidate worker, start a throwaway chat and a long-running Monitor shell that prints a marker and waits for an explicit release file in its disposable folder. As the authenticated owner, open the read-only Monitor viewer, wait for the marker and repeatedly disconnect and reconnect it at least 50 times while the worker is busy. Include abrupt WebSocket closes overlapping an owner-auth recheck. Reattach and inspect the same task's status/output after each disconnect. With a second owner login available for cleanup, revoke the viewer's owner session while attached and confirm the connection closes. Inspect worker logs for every connection, then release only the throwaway shell and archive its chat; do not stop or restart the worker.
rows.pass_when: Every disconnect and reconnect leaves the original shell running with the same task id and readable backlog. Revocation closes the viewer with code 4001 without stopping that shell. Worker logs contain no teardown exception, CancelledError or leaked Monitor connection task for these connections. The explicit release ends the shell normally; a missing log inspection or fewer than 50 disconnects is not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #402: a disconnect followed by ASGI cancellation during Monitor child-task cleanup propagated a child CancelledError through WebSocket teardown.

rows.check: Learned prose workflow across separately synthesized sessions
rows.how: Use a disposable local-owner Fluid install and project, never the installed worker's skill store. Complete the same harmless fixture-summary workflow in two separate non-code sessions, confirming each completed result with the exact user receipt workflow accepted: fixture-summary. Let synthesis drain after each session. Inspect fluid workflows list/show in a separate owner terminal. Before approval verify a fresh session cannot discover the skill; attempt approval from a managed agent shell and verify refusal. In the owner terminal approve the exact reviewed digest, then start fresh native and delegated sessions, load Skill(fixture-summary), and summarize a new fixture result. In another disposable project repeat with workflow corrected: fixture-summary or reject the proposal before approval. Remove only these disposable installs/projects.
rows.pass_when: The second synthesis creates one pending, project-scoped proposal with two source session IDs, ordered successful steps and evidence hashes, without installing it or adding another synthesis call. Only separate interactive local-owner approval installs SKILL.md. Fresh native and delegated sessions discover/load it and use its Checked: format for the new result. Corrected/rejected, private-path, secret-bearing and duplicate workflows do not promote. API-owned stores remain fail-closed pending an authenticated approval surface; this is not a test of an app approval UI.
rows.past_bug: #206: separately consumed journal slices could not ground repeated prose workflow proposals, although same-slice synthesis and manual promotion tests passed.

rows.how: On a disposable Linux/glibc candidate install only, grow a native session beyond 8 MiB of durable message JSON using streaming turns and tool results, then compact it. Repeatedly detach/reconnect that session and complete a turn, at least 60 seconds apart, with three clients attached. Sample fixed-process anonymous RSS, retained nodes, compaction residency, subscriber and task counts for 30 minutes after warm-up. Open old history and a fork ending before a checkpoint. Do not restart or instrument an installed worker.
rows.pass_when: The resumed transcript and older fork remain readable with unchanged compacted output. Retained nodes stay near the checkpoint tail and superseded digest residency does not increase on each reconnect. Warm anonymous RSS does not ratchet after large cold loads; only the first terminal after an evicted cold load may attempt allocator reclamation, globally at most once per minute. Ordinary turns do not trim; non-glibc and non-Linux workers remain unaffected.
rows.past_bug: #264: cold resume retained retired compaction entries after windowing and left large temporary transcript allocations in glibc arenas.

rows.check: ChatGPT Settings default and Included choice obey admission
rows.how: On a disposable candidate install only with a verified ChatGPT subscription, select the legacy ChatGPT Settings image default and clear remembered and job-stored image choices. Capture legacy-handler entry, cap/reservation state and provider-submission activity. First request one image through generateImage without source/model in a fresh interactive owner chat, leaving the choice card unanswered; repeat in an unattended automation with no job choice. Inspect structured results and confirm zero submissions. Next deliberately remember a verified Included ChatGPT choice with its exact account/model/holding worker. Using disposable fixture storage, establish recorded daily spend above the enabled daily cap without making paid calls, and confirm the cap is exhausted. Repeat the interactive and unattended image requests and inspect their structured results, cap/reservation state and provider activity. Restore only the disposable settings, choices, cap and fixture storage and archive the throwaway sessions. Never change an installed owner's preferences or ledger; no generation submission is authorized by this row.
rows.pass_when: With no stored choice the interactive result is choose with a choice card and the unattended result is skipped with reason no_stored_choice; neither request enters the legacy handler, reserves a generation or submits to any provider. With the stored Included choice and exhausted cap, both requests are refused with reason daily_cap and the unattended run reports it. Both refusals retain Included pricing (known USD zero), append no successful reservation and submit nothing. Retain structured results and zero-submission evidence; prose-only promises to ask or refuse are not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #379: the non-chat ChatGPT Settings default returned the legacy handler before the resolver, bypassing deliberate choices, Included pricing and daily-cap admission.

rows.check: Scheduled automation binds its stored choice on the holding worker
rows.how: Use disposable candidate workers ServerWorker and DesktopWorker with one owner-approved, verified Included image account held only by DesktopWorker. On ServerWorker create a disabled throwaway automation and PUT its exact account/worker/model/options to /api/v1/generation/jobs/{automation_id}/choices/image; GET it back. Leave remembered image choices empty or deliberately different. With the disposable cap admitting the request, trigger one scheduled run on ServerWorker with a prompt that calls generateImage without naming source/model/worker. Inspect the scheduler-created session's automation_id, structured generation result, both workers' submission activity and the resulting session artifact. Restore the disposable choices and remove only the throwaway automation/session afterward. No API-key or fal generation is authorized by this check.
rows.pass_when: The real unattended run uses the saved job choice despite the absent or different remembered choice. Result source/account/model/options and holding worker match the read-back binding; exactly one Included submission occurs on DesktopWorker, none on ServerWorker or another source. Current cap and schema admission run before submission, and the generated artifact is readable from the run session. A fixture that only injects RunContext.job_choices is not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #379: resolver support for job_choice had no production writer or binding from scheduled automation sessions.
